features.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly cite a specific real-world example (a named or concretely identifiable real case, event, person, study or situation) as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific, concrete real-world example (e.g., a named or identifiable real event, person, organization, place, study, statistic from a particular source, or a concretely described real case) in support of its argument; return 0 if none does (generic claims, hypotheticals, and vague 'some people' statements do not count). A cited external example counts as support even if the commenter did not experience it. Ignore any text that announces the OP's view change, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates, and do not treat them as examples. Use only OC_comments. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

h0: There is no association between any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example and the likelihood of OP view change.
h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example equal to 1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change than those with 0.
note: Operationalized "featuring" as at least one counter-comment citing a specific real-world example (any, not share/count). Comment order/timing unknown; comments may contain outcome-related text, which is excluded from the semantic judgment. Association only, not causal. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model.
